name: Cavineña
catalog_quote: Primary stress is always on the penultimate syllable and secondary stresses are reported on alternating syllables leftward (Key 1968:25)

audit.recode_to: Drop 'fixed-strict penult with alternating leftward secondaries (stress placement coded per word length as 10 010 1010 01010 (1 = a stressed syllable))'. reclassify per Guillaume 2008:41-42 (restated verbatim in held halshs-02527795v2 p.10) as a non-contrastive, word-delimiting pitch(-accent)/mixed stress-tone system: High assigned to the FIRST syllable and spreading rightward to every syllable before the last two, last two syllables Mid (prominence grid stress placement coded per word length as 10 100 1100 11100 111100 (1 = a stressed syllable)), no alternating secondary stresses; i.e. fixed: initial syllable pitch accent (or the catalog's 'no stress / delimitative word tone' kind if it has one), with a caution note that the SIL tradition (Key 1968:25; Liccardi 1983; Camp & Liccardi 1989:267) instead reports penultimate accent. At minimum, if the catalog keeps a stress reading, remove the alternating secondaries (attested only via Key 1968 second-hand) and mark the primary location contested (penult per SIL vs initial-H per Guillaume).

sources.quote: Camp & Liccardi (Spanish): "Since the accent always remains on the penultimate syllable (the one before the last), the addition of a monosyllabic enclitic makes the accent move to what would have been the last syllable." (Guillaume quotes are English.)
sources.note: The definitive modern grammar; its accent rule (initial High spreading to all but the last two syllables; pitch only, non-contrastive, delimitative) contradicts our Key-1968-based penult+alternating coding at every length >=3, and pp. 41-46 reportedly discuss the earlier penult-stress analyses (Key 1968, Liccardi 1983) — needed to reclassify with a verbatim quote and locator.

sources.quote: 'Como el acento siempre permanece en la penúltima sílaba (la que está antes de la última), la agregación de un enclítico monosilábico hace que el acento se mueva a la que habría sido la última sílaba, si el enclítico no estuviera allí como etáre casa a etaréju en la casa.' Refers readers to Liccardi 1983 (Notas Lingüísticas de Bolivia 12) for phonology.
